messages:
Maya: Hey team, customer Aisha from AcmePay opened a high-severity ticket — their integration started seeing a flurry of 502/504s from the hosted inference gateway around 14:02 UTC. They've pinned a couple of request IDs: req_3fa9a2, req_3fa9f0, req_3fb023. They say it started after a peak traffic spike and is reproducible from their side.

Aisha: Confirming — we saw 502 for ~8% of requests between 14:02-14:08. SDK retries didn't help, we ended up with duplicated user events. Here is the curl we used: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","input":"invoice summary"}'
```

Maya: Thanks. Attaching AcmePay account id: acct_8932. They are on hosted tier with default retry settings.

Jon M: I'm on it. Can you paste the raw response for one of the 502s, and the x-request-id header if available? Also what model/route latency looked like right before spike?

Aisha: Pasting the JSON snippet we captured: 

```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "gateway_error",
    "message": "Upstream timeout",
    "code": 502
  },
  "x-request-id": "req_3fa9a2"
}
```

Carlos: Noted. Two quick hypotheses: (1) routing/backpressure at gateway during short GPU pool saturation, (2) a model instance OOM/restart leading to transient 502s. Can we get logs from the runtime for those request IDs?

Maya: I already requested logs from hosted-logs for those IDs and pushed traces to the ticket. Support console shows a small increase in average queue time from 11ms to 220ms at 14:01:50 UTC.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary deployment of runtime-hotfix-2026-02 at 13:55 UTC completed on region us-west-2.

Priya: If there's a canary earlier, maybe we're seeing mismatched kernel selection for that build under certain sequence lengths. Carlos, can you correlate kernel metrics with those times?

Carlos: Will check. Also, did the customer use streaming? They said not. If they sent long prompt and we misestimate tokenization, KV cache pressure could grow. Aisha, do you have sample input with token counts?

Aisha: Sample payload (redacted): prompt is ~1200 chars, approx 200 tokens. No streaming. Small batch concurrency ~4.

Jon M: I pulled metrics from the gateway: at 14:02 there was a short spike in 5xxs across multiple customers (~0.6% of traffic), concentrated in a few routes hitting the same runtime pool. The runtime logs show a sequence of "connection reset by peer" from runtime->model process around 14:01:58 for a subset of pods. Likely process crash and restart causing upstream 502s.

Carlos: That aligns with OOM/restart. I'm checking pod logs now. Found repeated GC/oom-kill logs on pod runtime-prod-42. Stack: `killed process 4321 (runtime-worker)` with exit code -9. Similar traces for runtime-prod-43.

Maya: Escalating to eng-runtime for immediate mitigation. Priority: restore stable routing and avoid duplicate user events.

Carlos: Mitigation steps I propose now: (1) mark affected runtime pool unhealthy to stop routing new requests (2) spin up replacement pods with higher memory headroom and lighter batch configs (3) add temporary circuit-breaker at gateway for requeues to avoid client-level duplicate events.

Priya: For (3) we can adjust the SDK retry guidance in the short term: set max_retries=1 and backoff_ms=500 for hosted tier. I'll draft a KB note for customers.

Jon M: Implemented step (1) and (2) at 14:12 UTC — drained runtime-prod-42/43 and replaced with runtime-prod-88/89 with 20% more memory. Traffic backfilled at 14:14 UTC. 

Maya: Notified customer of steps and asked them to reduce retries until we confirm stable. They acknowledged and paused their background job at 14:15.

incidents-bot: [incident] New incident created: #INC-2026-113 - Hosted inference upstream timeouts (502/504) - severity P2.

Carlos: After replacements, 5xx rate returned to baseline by 14:20. Looking at pod metrics, the OOMs were triggered by a bad combination of batch size and an edge-case attention kernel in runtime-hotfix-2026-02. Patch ready to revert that kernel selection.

Jon M: Recommend rollback of the canary kernel selection to stable profile. I'll coordinate with deploy to avoid double rollback risk.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Rolling back runtime-hotfix-2026-02 kernel patch in us-west-2 at 14:28 UTC.

Priya: I'll prepare a short customer comms template: "We've mitigated the root cause (runtime kernel selection leading to OOMs) and rolled back the canary. Please resume normal operations; if you see further 502/504s, reach out immediately." Maya, can you send?

Maya: Sent to Aisha at 14:32. She responded: "Thanks, seeing normal traffic now on our end — will monitor"

Aisha: Quick follow-up — our logs show a couple of duplicated events during retry storm window. What's the recommended way to avoid duplicates when transient 5xx occurs?

Priya: Recommend idempotency keys on your side for non-idempotent operations, and set SDK retry to single attempt for synchronous flows. We'll publish a KB with examples (node/python).

Carlos: Action items for eng-runtime: 1) revert kernel selection canary (done), 2) add preflight memory check to pod startup to avoid launching with unsafe batch config, 3) add enhanced logging to correlate req_ids to pod restarts.

Jon M: Action items for SRE: 1) add alert on short-lived OOM spikes per runtime pool, 2) implement temporary circuit-breaker rule at gateway to fail-fast and return 429 instead of retrying into bad pool.

Maya: Support actions: 1) update KB and send to affected customers, 2) advise default SDK retry change for hosted customers while we stabilize.

Carlos: I'll follow up with a postmortem draft tomorrow with root cause analysis and mitigation timeline.

Maya: Closing loop — postmortem PR link: https://redwood.internal/pmr/INC-2026-113 (will add timeline + customer comms).

Aisha: Appreciate the quick response and the rollback. Marking ticket resolved on our end, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Jon M: Final note — we should audit other regions for canary rollout safety. There was a localized canary in us-west-2 that hit prod traffic. We'll tighten canary rules.

Carlos: Understood. Will include rollout guardrails in the postmortem.

Maya: Thanks team. I'll update the ticket and KB. If anything else crops up, re-open thread.
